title: Multiply Strings
prompt:
Given two non-negative integers `num1` and `num2` as strings, return their product as a string. You may not use a big-integer library or convert the inputs to integers directly.

**Example**: `"123" × "456"` → `"56088"`.

**Constraints**: `1 ≤ num1.length, num2.length ≤ 200`; no leading zeros except `"0"` itself.
hints: How many digits can the product of an m-digit number and an n-digit number have? Could you fill an array of that size digit by digit?
Do long multiplication from the right: multiply every digit pair and add each product into the correct slot of an `int[m + n]`, carrying as you go.
Digit i × digit j: `sum = product + pos[i+j+1]; pos[i+j+1] = sum % 10; pos[i+j] += sum / 10;`. Then skip leading zeros when you build the string.

solution.explanation: Digit i of num1 (counted from the left) times digit j of num2 has its ones digit at result position i+j+1 and its carry at i+j. So every partial product can be added into one array with no shifting. Going right to left pushes carries left as you go, and a final pass drops leading zeros. O(m·n) time, O(m+n) space.
